To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a mobile robot can be successfully navigated in an indoor environment using a partially-observable controller that relies on noisy RSS measurements emitted by RFID beacons.
we have developed a novel controller that can be used to track a desired trajectory of a mobile robot using noisy received signal strength (RS) measurements emitted from a group of RFID tags.
we propose a novel control scheme for trajectory tracking of a mobile robot using noisy RSS measurements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an autonomous navigation system for a mobile robot in an indoor environment using RFID technology.
a new class of mobile robot controllers that can be used for indoor navigation using RFID tags.
the development of a novel controller for a wheel mobile robot that is capable of tracking a given reference trajectory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the controller performance is satisfactory in the presence of noisy RSS measurements.

the controller presented in this paper is able to track the reference trajectory in the presence of noise, and that the performance of the controller is robust to noise and the robot model uncertainties.
the controller performance is very good in the sense that it is able to track the desired trajectory with very small error.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a robot can be guided to a target location in a noisy environment by using only noisy RSS measurements emitted by RFID tags, without the need of any other sensors.
we have proposed a novel approach for mobile robot navigation using RSS measurements from RFIDs.

we have developed a controller that can navigate a mobile robot in an indoor environment using RSS measurements emitted from RFID tags, where the controller performance is independent of the RSS measurements accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to achieve accurate mobile robot navigation using RSS measurements from RFID tags without any knowledge of the RSS-to-distance mapping.
the proposed controller can achieve accurate trajectory tracking in reverberant indoor environments using noisy RSS measurements from RFID tags.
the proposed controller can track a desired trajectory using only the RSS measurements, which are not necessarily LOS distances, and without any knowledge about the robot model.
